speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are presenting with acute diarrhea; to determine the underlying cause, please tell me when your symptoms began and if you have had any recent travel or sick contacts. Additionally, have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool, or experienced a high fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea (likely *Clostridioides difficile* infection).

Given your recent use of levofloxacin for pneumonia and the severity of your watery diarrhea (9 episodes in two days) with abdominal cramping, this is highly suspicious for *C. diff*. I need to confirm if you have a fever or history of hospitalization. I will immediately order a stool test to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: C.diff_toxin_stool_assay
